clue.text: Can I get in finally as classics student?

indicators.note: to get in is to be put inside, so the can and the I go within the word for finally

parts.note: at last, so finally gives LAST
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they will at last be accepted as a student of the classics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the noun TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latinist is a scholar of the Latin language and literature, a core classical subject.

clue.text: Yorkshire banker entertains good egg

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the river takes the letter inside

parts.note: a banker is something with banks, a river; the Ure flows through Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire bank manager plays host to a decent sort of chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword code for a river, here the Ure in North Yorkshire. 'Egg' is the verb, as in egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to encourage or press them, the same as to urge them.

clue.text: Persian ass runs on time to come first

indicators.note: this says the on-plus-time pair is placed ahead of the runs letter in the answer

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A donkey from Persia keeps running on, as if determined to finish first.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass of Iran and neighbouring Asia, so a Persian ass is an example.

clue.text: Say canal inspector — in London's Hampstead?

definitions.text: Say canal inspector — in London's Hampstead?

parts.words: Say canal inspector — in London's Hampstead?
parts.note: a root canal is dental work, so its inspector works on teeth; Hampstead Heath is cockney rhyming slang for teeth, so the inspector of Hampsteads is a tooth doctor

explanation.surface: Someone checks waterways around Hampstead, a well-heeled district of north London.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is a root canal, not a waterway. In cockney rhyming slang 'Hampsteads' (from Hampstead Heath) means teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon examines root canals and teeth, playfully called an inspector of them.

clue.text: Koran has to be revised, requiring craft in religion

indicators.note: a text to be revised will be reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demand that the Koran be revised, as religion needs some craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be revised' rearranges KORAN HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel built by Noah in Genesis is a boat famous from scripture, a craft in religion.

clue.text: It's spread, by fool covering dead

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the fool word goes around the dead word

parts.note: to cod is to hoax or fool someone
the late king is the dead king

explanation.surface: Something has been smeared about by a clown who is covering up a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' is the verb cod, to hoax, and 'dead' is late as in the late king; 'It's spread' reads as 'it has percolated'.
explanation.definitionFit: News that has percolated has filtered through gradually, i.e. spread among people.

clue.text: Over half these clues!

definitions.meaning: over in the sense of to the far side, as in walk over the road
a crossword's clues are split into two lists, one of which is the horizontal lot

explanation.surface: A setter's sigh that half the puzzle has been dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: Across means over to the other side, and also labels the horizontal half of a crossword's clues.

clue.text: He wrote fine stuff about enlisted woman

indicators.note: about means around, so the fabric goes around the servicewoman

parts.note: lace is a fine, delicate fabric
a Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service

explanation.surface: A writer pens something exquisite about a woman who has joined up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He wrote' defines a writer: D. H. Lawrence or T. E. Lawrence. A Wren is a member of the WRNS, the British women's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence was a novelist, so the answer names a man who wrote.

clue.text: High-octane plays like these can be short

definitions.text: plays like these can be short

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Plays written in a high-octane style are often short, punchy pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like part of the compound 'High-octane', but it signals that OCTANE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama in a single act is by nature brief, so plays of this kind are short.

clue.text: Racketeer Mike to be buried outside

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the burial word goes round the letter

parts.note: the dead lie in their graves
Mike is the radio code word for the letter M

explanation.surface: A gangster named Mike is to be killed and buried somewhere outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lime is the black-market racketeer in the film The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Lime, played by Orson Welles, sells diluted penicillin in post-war Vienna, a classic criminal racketeer.

clue.text: Perhaps to lose your head is to lose your job

definitions.meaning: to be beheaded by the axe, an example of a literal fatal cut
to be dismissed or sacked from work

explanation.surface: Losing your head is, figuratively, as bad as being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being dismissed, and taken literally it means being executed by the axe.

clue.text: Secret writing method an unimportant thing

definitions.meaning: a nonentity or nought, someone or something of no account

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that some code is not worth bothering with.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a code system and zero, hence a person or thing of no value.

clue.text: Sect member's exclusively spoken with bird

indicators.note: spoken means said out loud, so the word for exclusively is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: wholly means entirely, exclusively
the roller is a colourful crow-sized bird

explanation.surface: A cult member talks only with a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns WHOLLY into its sound-alike HOLY; the 's of 'member's' is the link 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecostal worshippers given to ecstatic, writhing displays were nicknamed after this behaviour, so one is a sect member.

clue.text: Black Jack on losing little weight in three seconds

indicators.note: in places the sailor and the trimmed side inside the three letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, taken three times
a jack tar is a sailor, so Jack gives TAR

indicators.note: losing means dropping, so the weight letter is taken out of the cricket side

parts.note: on and leg are the same side of the field in cricket
G is the abbreviation for gram, a small weight

explanation.surface: A man called Jack tries a crash diet, shedding a little weight in a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' gives LEG; 'losing little weight' drops G to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A night sky without visible stars is pitch dark, so starless can mean black.

clue.text: Immense rook goes after girl

indicators.note: goes after means follows, so the chess letter is placed behind the name

parts.note: Stella is a girl's name
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A huge rook chases a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the stars and so on an astronomical scale, the word is used for something outstanding or vast.

clue.text: Queen wants swan girl put up by assistant

indicators.note: in a down clue putting up a word raises it, so it is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Leda was seduced by Zeus in the form of a swan
an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A queen asks that a girl with a swan be put up next to her helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses LEDA to ADEL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide was the consort of William IV, a British queen after whom the Australian city is named.

clue.text: Anything but concrete boat put into Seychelles

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the boat sits within the country code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A boat made of concrete is sailed into the Seychelles, which seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the building material but means definite.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy plans are vague and lacking detail, the opposite of concrete, definite ones.

clue.text: Well-proportioned worker on unknown amount

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farm hand
some means an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: A worker is paid an unknown sum, and the result is well-proportioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome, applied to a building or figure, means of fine, balanced build and pleasing form.

clue.text: United including only men in position to perform

indicators.note: including means containing, so the united word holds the men-only word

parts.note: people united are as one
a stag party is for men only

explanation.surface: A football team, United, fielding only men is ready to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, but it means ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is in front of the audience on the boards is in place to perform.

indicators.note: the 22 Across answer means concealed, so it tells us to find a word tucked inside the run of referenced answers

parts.note: these refer to the answers of 1 Down, 2 Down and 3 Down, written one after another

explanation.surface: The clue is only a string of cross-references, with no surface to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 Across answer means concealed, so the solution lies within the 1, 2 and 3 Down answers run together; 24 Down's answer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The large caviar-yielding river creature is a kind of fish, the 24 Down answer.

clue.text: Smallest room that can be hired accommodates one

indicators.note: accommodates means houses, so the letter for one goes inside the hiring phrase

parts.note: a property that can be hired is to let
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tiny rented flat whose smallest room holds only one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The lavatory is jokingly known in Britain as the smallest room in the house.

clue.text: Concealed serious defeat

definitions.meaning: hidden away, as in staying out of sight
a thrashing or trouncing, as in getting a good beating

explanation.surface: A heavy defeat was hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding means lying concealed, and a hiding is a thrashing, a heavy defeat.

clue.text: Acclaim classic drama featured in 60 Minutes

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the drama goes within the time span

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour
Noh is the classical Japanese masked drama, also spelt No

explanation.surface: A TV news show, 60 Minutes, praises a classic play.
explanation.walkthrough: '60 Minutes' looks like the American TV programme but is just a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone is to praise and celebrate them publicly, i.e. acclaim them.

clue.text: American player's ball-point used to pen vote

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as a pen holds sheep, so the shuffled letters surround the voting mark
used in the sense of worn and knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: An American actor has a ballpoint used to sign his vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' rearranges BALLPOINT into BILLPATON, and 'to pen' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This film actor from Texas starred in Aliens, Apollo 13 and Twister, so he was an American player.

clue.text: Large, having consumed seconds, go without food

indicators.note: having eaten something takes it inside, so the large word swallows the letter

parts.note: fat means large in girth

explanation.surface: A large person who went back for seconds now has to diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like second helpings but is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from eating, usually for religious or health reasons.

clue.text: Folio is top for highbrow school population

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so the opening letter of highbrow is taken

explanation.surface: A folio is the top choice for the brainy pupils of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of swimming creatures, not a place of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish swim in schools, so they make up the population of a school.

clue.text: Maybe Arthur was in van ferrying dope

indicators.note: ferrying means carrying, so the leading word holds the information word

parts.note: to be in the van (vanguard) is to be at the front, so to have led
dope and gen both mean information

explanation.surface: Someone says Arthur was in a van that was carrying drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' is short for vanguard, and 'dope' means inside information, not drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur is a figure of myth and story, an example of a hero of folklore.

clue.text: Ruined morgues Poe's last inspiring horror

definitions.note: used attributively, as in a horror story, so it stands for an adjective

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the rearranged letters take in the final letter
a ruined thing is broken up, so these letters are rearranged
last picks the final letter of Poe's name

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe's final tale is set in crumbling mortuaries, a classic of horror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' rearranges MORGUES and 'inspiring' takes E (the last letter of Poe) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Grisly and ghastly things are the stuff of horror stories, so the adjective fits the genre.
